claims.text: Surtsey, an uninhabited volcanic island off the southern coast of Iceland, is the southernmost point of Iceland.
The eruption that formed Surtsey began 130 metres below sea level and reached the surface on 14 November 1963.
The eruption lasted until 5 June 1967, when the island reached its maximum size of 2.7 km2.
After just a few days the new island measured over 500 metres in length and had reached a height of 45 metres.
Wave erosion has steadily diminished the island: as of 2012 its surface area was 1.3 km2.
The island's highest point was 174 metres above sea level when the eruption ended; the most recent survey (2007) shows 155 metres.
Two other islands formed beside it, Syrtlingur in 1965 and Jólnir in 1965-66, and both were worn away by the waves and dropped below sea level.
In the spring of 1965 the first vascular plant, Cakile arctica, was found growing on the northern shore of Surtsey.
Surtsey was declared a nature reserve in 1965, and today only a few scientists are permitted to land on it.
In 2008 UNESCO declared the island a World Heritage Site.
